_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: Taylor published the terms of a proposed data center campus agreement before the council vote. They set its buildings, noise and water against what would apply without the agreement.

introduction.text: [The City of Taylor says it is considering a proposed agreement with Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers covering annexation and development of Taylor Technology Campus](c1). [The city describes it as a {{number:c2}}-acre project with data center facilities and on-site power generation](c2), [immediately east of the current city limits](c3). [The agreement still has to go before the City Council for a vote on {{date:c4}}](c4).

[The developers withdrew their annexation and zoning application on {{date:c6}}](c6). [The city says that without the agreement the project would have stayed in unincorporated Williamson County, which has no zoning authority](c8). [It says it would then have had no authority over any aspect of the project](c9).

sections.heading: What the terms set, in feet

paragraphs.text: [Buildings would sit at least {{number:c30}} feet from the north, east and west property lines](c30). [Along the south line, data centers, power generation and battery storage would sit at least {{number:c31}} feet back, and accessory structures at least {{number:c31:1}} feet](c31).

[A permanent landscaped buffer of at least {{number:c32}} feet would run along the south property line](c32). [It would carry earthen berms at least {{number:c33}} feet high for screening](c33). [The city says the landscaping and buffer areas would separate the development from nearby homes](c59).

[Noise from the development would be capped at the greater of {{number:c12}} dBA or the level before construction](c12). [An acoustic study at the property lines would set that level](c14). [Without the agreement the city's table lists the state limit of {{number:c13}} dBA](c13).

[Cooling would run in a closed loop on reclaimed water, with an initial fill of {{number:c17}} million gallons for the whole site](c17). [Drinking water would not fill the cooling system unless one of the agreement's exceptions applies](c19). [The first is a temporary emergency approved in writing by the city manager](c20). [The second applies if the city misses its deadline to build the reclaimed water improvements](c21). [The third applies if reclaimed service starts and is later cut below what the developers need](c22).

[The developers would commit {{money:c35}} for community investments and nonprofit support](c35). [They are not asking for any tax abatement](c43). [The city projects {{money:c44}} in gross tax revenue over {{number:c44:1}} years, which is its own projection and not a measured amount](c44).

[In June a coalition of residents presented the city with a petition at a council meeting, calling for a temporary ban on new data center development in Taylor](c50). [KEYE reported that the coalition gathered about {{number:c52}} signatures](c52). [KEYE also reported that the city found the petition can't go on the ballot, because Texas law doesn't allow zoning changes by popular vote](c51). [Texas Standard reported that coalition members filed a motion with the Third Court of Appeals](c54). [The motion claims the city and its council violated the Texas Open Meetings Act and the city charter by not acting on the proposed ban](c54).

sections.heading: What the record does not yet show

paragraphs.text: [The agreement is a proposal awaiting the council's vote](c4), and the terms here are the city's own summary of it. The city's pages cited here give no size for the buildings. [The noise cap rises above {{number:c12}} dBA only if an acoustic study at the property lines measures a higher level before construction](c12). That study's result is not in the documents cited here.

[Spectrum News reported on {{date:c55}} that the Texas attorney general's office is investigating a proposed data center in Taylor](c55). [Spectrum identifies that developer as Blueprint Data Centers, a separate project from Taylor Technology Campus](c56).
